target_customer: Consumers (search users, then celebrity fans); no clear paying customer
problem: Search engines were slow to surface content as it was shared on social sites. After the pivot, fans had no easy way to see where celebrities were at a given moment.
business_model: Free consumer web service, no revenue model documented in sources
product_category: Real-time social search, then celebrity sighting tracker

founders.name: AJ Asver
founders.background_notes: Named as co-creator of Scoopler in 2009 coverage.

founders.name: Dilan Jayawardane
founders.background_notes: Spelled Jarawardane on the YC page.

founders.name: Benjamin Tauber
founders.background_notes: Crunchbase lists him as COO and founder; joined the team around the JustSpotted period.

exit.reason: Press describes an acquihire of the team for Google+, not a purchase of the business; both services were shut down.

competitors.name: OneRiot
competitors.what: Real-time search that crawled links shared on Twitter, Digg and other services
competitors.traction_then: Over one million queries a day by Sept 2009
competitors.funding_then: Raised about $7M per a Vator headline

competitors.name: Collecta
competitors.what: Real-time search over Twitter, news feeds, blogs, comments and Flickr

competitors.name: Twitter Search
competitors.what: Native search over tweets, which Scoopler results were said to resemble

technical_complexity.rationale: Indexing live streams from several services and updating results in the browser without refresh needed custom search architecture, which coverage says the team built in 2009.

defensibility.rationale: Results depended on third party feeds and Twitter access. Several rivals launched near the same time, and the pivot to celebrity tracking aggregated public data.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Reporting says Twitter cut off firehose access after the pivot, and Google hired the team in July 2011 and the services closed.

market_need_then: Twitter and social sharing were growing fast in 2009 and trade press ran many stories on real-time search as the next search frontier, though the same press noted most entrants fizzled.

identity.voice_and_tone: YC copy for JustSpotted is playful and fan oriented (connecting with celebs).

rebrands.why: Pivot from real-time search to celebrity tracking; no stated brand rationale found.

brand_strength.rationale: Coverage focuses on the product and the Google hire. No sources found on logo, merch or community. The rename was a total change after a brand had been built.

pivots.why: Not stated in sources found; press says Twitter later cut off Scoopler's firehose access after the pivot.

outcome_analysis: Scoopler entered a crowded real-time search field in 2009, raised a small seed from Ron Conway, Michael Birch and Avalon, then pivoted in 2010 to celebrity sightings. The pivot did not produce a lasting product. Google hired the three founders in July 2011 for Google+ and both services were closed, so the directory label of acquired is better read as a soft landing. The cause of the shutdown beyond the hire is not public.
notes: Seed amount not stated in the sources seen. CB Insights lists about 770K over four rounds, unverified, and a TechCrunch author guessed near 1M total, so no amount recorded. justspotted.com did not resolve from the session. Mergr date of June 2011 conflicts with July 2011 press. Founder backgrounds not found.
